header.running_head: Being Stern with those who Oppose the Commands of Rasulullaah ﷺ

blocks.text:

This time, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I prefer that he meets Allaah beneath the lash rather than me meeting Allaah with the responsibility of lashing him still on my shoulders. Bring me a strong whip." (When the whip was brought) Hadhrat Umar (RA) gave the instruction and Hadhrat Qudaamah (RA) was lashed.
Hadhrat Umar (RA) was then angry with Hadhrat Qudaamah (RA) and broke off ties with him. Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Qudaamah (RA) later both performed Hajj while Hadhrat Umar (RA) was still angry with Hadhrat Qudaamah (RA). When they were both returning from the Hajj, Hadhrat Umar (RA) camped at a place called Suqya, where he fell asleep. When he awoke, from his sleep, he said, "Bring Qudaamah to me quickly. By Allaah! Someone came to me in my dream saying, 'Reconcile with Qudaamah because he is your brother.' Bring him to me quickly." When the people went to Hadhrat Qudaamah (RA), he refused to go. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then instructed them to bring him by force. (When he arrived) Hadhrat Umar (RA) then spoke to him and sought Allaah's forgiveness for him.[^1]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Rebukes Someone Laughing during a Funeral

Hadhrat Yazeed bin Ubaydullaah reports from some of his companions that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) once saw a man laughing at a funeral. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said to him, "Are you laughing while you are at a funeral? By Allaah! I shall never speak to you again."[^2]
The Fear of the Sahabah (RA) when An Instruction of Rasulullaah ﷺ was Opposed
Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfah (RA) Fears Something he said during the Battle of Badr

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that on the day the Battle of Badr of was fought, Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the Sahabah (RA), "I know well that the men from the Banu Haashim were forced to march and have no desire to fight against us. Therefore, whoever confronts anyone from the Banu Haashim should not kill him. Whoever confronts Abul Bakhtari bin Hishaam bin Haarith bin Asad should not kill him and whoever of you confronts Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib the uncle of Rasulullaah ﷺ should also not kill him because he had been forced (to fight)." At this, Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfah bin Utba bin Rabee'ah (RA) said, "Should we kill our fathers, our sons and our brothers and leave Abbaas? By Allaah! If I happen to confront Abbaas, I shall cut him to pieces with my sword."
Abdur Razzaaq and Abu Ali bin Sakan, as quoted in Isaabah (Vol.3 Pg.229).
Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.116).
